classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b scaffold the without-replacement idea. The student only updates the counts after removals (9 pens with 4 blue; 8 pens with 5 red) and reads off a single fraction. Part c then chains the three probabilities by multiplication, and the first factor, 6/10, is the only one not already found. This is slightly harder than the direct independent products in p19-practice-block, because the changing denominators and tracking of which colours have been removed need care. It is easier than p29-q8, which adds a tree structure, several multiplied branches and a complement step. There is no hidden insight and no complement or multiple-ordering decision. The hardest essential demand is a routine linked three-stage product.
